newsitem.title: UK: Greene King to shut brewery, takes provision.
newsitem.headline: Greene King to shut brewery, takes provision.

text.p: Pub and brewery group Greene King said it will close its brewery at Biggleswade and shut two distribution depots following a review of its brewing strategy, chairman David McCall said on Wednesday.
"We will need to write off a number of assets and there will also be some exceptional costs resulting from the restructuring," he said in a statement.

"Altogether a provision of about 14 million stg is likely to be made against the current year's profits, although the net cash outlay including capital expenditure is unlikely to exceed 8.0 million stg and will be spread over two financial years."

McCall said the company would prefer to sell Biggleswade as a working brewery in order to minimise job losses, but if it cannot then it plans to stop brewing in April and move off the site completely by the end of 1997.

The closure of its Biggleswade brewery in central England will also mean the relocation of its distribution operation in October to a new site to the west. The strategic review also resulted in the decision to close its Norwich depot in May and its Furneux Pelham depot in July 1997.

The planned restructuring will result in the loss of 130 jobs in brewing and distribution although Greene King created some 300 jobs in its pubs in 1996 and expects to generate a similar number in 1997.

The company plans to focus on its main ale brands -- Greene King IPA, Abbot Ale and Wexford -- and as a result will invest in its Bury St Edmunds brewery to install a new keg line and set-up a single integrated warehouse.
